svg.text: WHY UNDER-REPORTING IS THE REAL DANGER

g.text: Most needlestick injuries in busy wards are never reported: too busy, afraid of blame, or assumed low risk.
An injury that is not reported cannot be treated, cannot be counted, and cannot generate the case for supplies.
It is an occupational hazard to be prevented,
not an unavoidable part of the job. Report it,
and fix the waiting and the information that
Back injury ends nursing careers quietly.
Assess before lifting, use the equipment,

svg.text: A manager who cannot keep her staff safe will not keep her staff.
Every unreported injury is a warning the facility paid for and then threw away.
